notes:
Two sets (synonymity, directional) use symmetric pairs that read the same in either order, failing the order-indistinguishable check. Fix by replacing one pair in each set with a directional variant within the selkie-shore world.
- set-synonymity: Synonym pairs (selkie:seal-folk, pelt:hide) are mutually reversible — car:auto reads the same as auto:car, so order carries no signal.
  Try: Change the relationship to a directional one, e.g. 'formal term : folk term' — keep selkie:seal-folk (formal myth-name : common name) and replace pelt:hide with sealskin:coat (the specific magical garment vs. the everyday word for it), fixing direction formal-to-casual.
  Or: Replace pelt:hide with a non-symmetric pair from the same skin-vocabulary, such as sealskin:garment, where sealskin is the specific folklore term and garment is the generic term it's referred to as once worn.
  Or: If synonymity must stay symmetric, relabel the relationship as 'two names for the same thing (order-free)' and have the board-builder mark this set as intentionally non-directional rather than fixing word choice.
- set-directional: Shoreline:horizon and surface:seabed are axis-endpoint pairs with no inherent start — back:front reads the same as front:back, so the order is unrecoverable.
  Try: Reframe as a near-to-far direction and keep it consistent: shoreline (near) : horizon (far), surface (near) : seabed (far) — this is already the intended reading, so lock it by changing the relationship label to 'near point : far point along a single axis' to make the direction explicit rather than swapping words.
  Or: Replace one pair to add an inherent sequence, e.g. swap surface:seabed for tideline:seabed, where tideline is explicitly the near/shallow marker and seabed the deep end, reinforcing a one-way reading the player can infer without guessing.
  Or: If no directional cue can be added via wording, change the relationship type entirely to something order-locked, e.g. 'cause then consequence' is not available here — safest is the near:far relabel plus confirming both pairs run shallow-to-deep rather than deep-to-shallow.
Do not change: set-enabling-agent, set-item-location — no allowlisted finding touches them.

persisted.note: Both halves read as 'mythical being : the name of its skin', so a player could reasonably solve it this way instead of as pure synonym pairs. Both halves read as: "selkie : the skin/covering associated with it (pelt)" and "seal-folk : the skin/covering associated with it (hide)".

Since pelt and hide are interchangeable skin-words, this swapped pairing still reads as 'being : its skin' on both sides. Both halves read as: "selkie : the skin/covering associated with it (hide)" and "seal-folk : the skin/covering associated with it (pelt)".
